suggestions.currentProposed: arc de tir à l’arc pour enfant
suggestions.reason: Arc de tir à l’arc is tautological in French because arc already names the bow; arc pour enfant is the natural catalog phrase.
Ranger is localized as Waldläufer in the German Tolkien context; the correction preserves Aragorn and forms a natural German product compound.
The character is localized as Grauer Wurm in German; the genitive phrase is grammatical and avoids an unnecessary English hybrid compound.
In camping-product terminology a small replaceable fuel canister is a cartuccia, whereas bombola normally denotes a larger gas cylinder.
Italian franchise usage localizes the character name as Verme Grigio; elmo remains the correct historical-armor term.
Juego 1 reads as Game 1; in an armor-set product attribute, Conjunto 1 preserves the intended set/group meaning.
The established Spanish franchise name is Gusano Gris; retaining the English name creates an avoidable mixed-language tag.

suggestions.currentProposed: arco infantil de tiro con arco
suggestions.reason: Tiro con arco after arco is repetitive; the correction is idiomatic Spanish and preserves both the shooting-bow and child-target meanings.
Natureza remota is an unnatural literal phrase; região selvagem naturally denotes a remote undeveloped backcountry area.
Portuguese franchise usage localizes the character as Verme Cinzento; the English name should not remain in a localized tag.
The storefront uses European Portuguese, where the canonical title is O Feiticeiro de Oz; Mágico de Oz is not the established title.
